newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines gets lead offers for Yankee bond float.
newsitem.headline: Philippines gets lead offers for Yankee bond float.

text.p: JP Morgan and CS First Boston have offered to lead manage a Yankee bond issue by the Philippine government for up to $1 billion with a 30-year maturity, the Central Bank said on Tuesday.
CS First Boston is the investment holding arm of CS Holding
CS First Boston Asia-Pacific chairman Stephen Stonefeld even offered to issue international bonds for the government "beyond 30 years," Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said in a statement.
The Central Bank earlier received offers for similar issues from Morgan Stanley, Salomon Brothers and ING Barings.

Singson said current market conditions offer the Central Bank an opportunity to raise long-term, low cost funds as U.S. yields, on whose rates the proposed issue would be based, were near all-time lows as of last Friday.
Manila hopes to use earnings from the issue to finance major infrastructure projects.
Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said last week the Philipines expected to make a Europeso or Yankee bond issue in the first half of 1997.
A committee evaluating the offers plans to submit its recommendation by early next year to the Central Bank's policy-making Monetary Board for decision, a bank official said.
